description: Search in a richer quaternionic perfect-sequence space and only later project to real binary shadows. If quaternionic phases cluster around low-defect real shadows more often than random binary starts do, they become a practical latent space for 668 search.
mathematical_formalization: Sample q in {+1,-1,+i,-i,+j,-j,+k,-k}^{167}. Define shadow maps Pi_alpha(q) in {+1,-1}^{4 x 167} by phase partitioning, score J(Pi_alpha(q)) by autocorrelation or modular defect, and run CA repair R_f on the best shadows.
analogical_connections: Latent-variable decoding from noncommutative phase space.
Proposal priors from a richer algebraic alphabet.
implementation_hypothesis: Enumerate or sample small quaternionic perfect sequences, evaluate several shadow maps, keep the maps with the best enrichment, and then push their real shadows through a CA repair loop.
experiment_seed: Compare quality distributions of projected quaternionic shadows and random real seeds on small exact targets and on 32- or 64-modular filters before scaling to length 167.

closest_prior_art.title: Quaternionic Perfect Sequences and Hadamard Matrices
Perfect Sequences and Arrays over the Unit Quaternions

novelty_claim: The novelty is a measured projection-and-repair pipeline from quaternionic latent space into real 668 candidate space, not a claim that quaternionic theory already solves the real case.
differentiation: Prior quaternionic work stays inside quaternionic sequence families. Here those families only serve as proposal generators for a real-domain search with explicit downstream repair and filtering.
